_comment: Per-invariant violation FLOORS for the reference sweep (ReferenceConfig: seeds 1..60 x 2000 steps x MaxWindows 12, DefaultConfig otherwise). cmd/fuzz-gate fails CI if any invariant EXCEEDS its floor, or if a brand-new invariant class (not listed here) appears. Floors are the CURRENT measured value so the gate is green now; each non-zero floor carries a justification so a reviewer can drive it down. Triage categories: (clean)=zero, genuine residual=0; (sim)=sim-model limitation artifact; (gen)=aggressive-generator artifact; (prod)=open production bug awaiting a fix. Update procedure: run `go run ./cmd/fuzz-gate -update` to regenerate, then justify any change in review.

justifications.no-crash: (clean) HandleEvent never panics. Floor 0 — any panic is a real bug.
justifications.no-invalid-cmd: (clean) sim never records an unsupported command. Floor 0.
justifications.no-sway-reject: (clean) sim never records a command real sway would refuse. Floor 0.
justifications.focus-convergence: (clean) at most one focused leaf after any step. Floor 0.
justifications.no-handler-error: (clean) no layout manager returns an Error-level failure. Floor 0.
justifications.maximized-fold-intact: (clean) REAL-bug class. A manager claiming maximized MUST actually be folded (master sharing the stack column, parent tabbed) — the shape toggleMaximize builds and the unmax branch assumes. Floor 0. This exists because `maximized` is an assertion-SUPPRESSION switch the manager owns: master-width-honored and master-stack-split both SKIP a maximized workspace, so a stale-true flag silently disables them — the bug and its own detector in one. That is how the 2026-07-16 state-drift bug (popWindow leaving the flag set after the fold collapsed) hid for hundreds of steps until an unmaximize replayed its restore against a never-folded tree.
justifications.master-width-honored: (clean) REAL-bug class: master width is only checked when the row is HEALTHY — the masters plus the stack column, nothing else. Floor 0. A master-width regression (e.g. reverting 6ae4d4a's stale-rect snapshot) drives this NON-ZERO (measured: 8 over this reference config). This is the gate's primary master-width signal. Held at 0 through both 2026-08-12 changes (moveDir fidelity, Tabbed strip rework), including on a 200-seed x 5000-step sweep, 3.3x the reference.
justifications.master-width-degenerate: (clean) FALSE-POSITIVE class split off from master-width-honored: the master's row is too broken for its width to mean anything — either a tracked stack window shares the master's parent (the master-stack-split bug shape) or the row holds windows the manager does not count as masters. Floor 0 on the reference sweep. The second rule was added 2026-08-12: a workspace that has been through a tabbed phase can leave every window in one row while the manager tracks only the few it adopted, and the old rule read that as 'healthy' and blamed the width. In such a crowd the sim's 1%-minimum clamp makes the target width unreachable outright (the tell is a `got` of exactly 1 - 0.01*(row-1)), so it is noise on top of a structural bug that master-stack-split already owns. Without the rule the deep sweep put 241 of these in the REAL class.
justifications.no-wrapper-chain: (sim+gen+prod) Persistent singleton-wrapper chains; cumulative-with-persistence, so one bad state recounts every step (1026 counts = 270 distinct runs). Raised 394 -> 906 on 2026-08-12 by the moveDir fidelity change (directional moves promote at an edge now, as sway does, so a raw `move left`/`move right` can strand a wrapper), then 906 -> 1026 by the Tabbed strip rework re-rolling every trajectory. The first reproducer (seed=1 step=203) is NOT a layout-manager bug but the hub's nativeSwayFallback: `nop tilekeeper move left workspace 7` on an UNMANAGED workspace forwards a scopeless `move left`, which sway applies to whatever is focused — a window on a DIFFERENT, managed workspace, restructuring it behind that manager's back. Guarding the fallback on 'the named workspace actually holds focus' measured 906 -> 624 when tried; left as a standalone follow-up. Remainder is the pre-existing MasterStack-flatten-foreign-trees gap.
justifications.tabbed-strip-flat: (gen+prod) Every tiled window on a Tabbed-managed workspace must be a tab in ONE flat strip. 412 counts = 215 distinct runs; lowered 481 -> 412 by the 2026-08-12 strip rework (Tabbed now builds the strip container by con id and gathers strays onto an anchor INSIDE it, so it no longer needs a workspace-direct leaf to repair a nested tree). The ws8 edge-move escape this class was written for contributes 0. What remains is cross-manager interference the generator manufactures: another workspace's MasterStack keeps tracking a window that moved here (the tracked-matches-leaves residual) and aims a `split none` at it, collapsing a one-tab strip into a bare window. Tabbed repairs on the next add or remove, so each occurrence is bounded, not permanent. Drive to 0 by fixing stale cross-workspace tracking, not by loosening this check.
justifications.tracked-matches-leaves: (sim+gen) Manager tracking vs sim leaf set. Cumulative-with-persistence: 67388 counts = 13056 distinct runs. Raised 38331 -> 47231 by the moveDir fidelity change and 47231 -> 67388 by the Tabbed strip rework. Driver of the second jump: with every window on a tabbed workspace now inside ONE strip container, genContainerWorkspaceMove — which relocates ws.Nodes[0] — moves that whole strip in a single op instead of one branch of a split, so each move strands a workspace's worth of fellow-travelers as untracked on the destination. That is the generator being maximally hostile, not a new production regression: the shape it exploits (one container per tabbed workspace) is the shape real sway builds. Largest residual; a manager-side fix is adopt-on-arrival for fellow-travelers, which handleWindowMove already does for the single-window case.
justifications.master-stack-split: (sim+gen+prod) Master shares its parent with a stack window (stack column missing). LOWERED 12967 -> 3785 on 2026-08-12 by the moveDir fidelity change (MasterStack extracts a promoted master with a bare `move <opposite-of-stack-side>`, which the old intra-parent sim model turned into a no-op, so the master stayed buried in the stack column for the rest of the walk), then 3785 -> 3519 by the Tabbed rework. Across the 200-seed x 5000-step sweep the class fell 105238 -> 27983, a 73% reduction against the pre-change baseline. Remainder is the aggressive workspace-move generator plus the MasterStack-not-flattening-foreign-trees follow-up. Residual ratchets re-baseline on a deliberate behavior change; floor-0 classes never do.
